### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 48 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7610545632400cd5f82fa392bb2676248312f305` — the merge of head `1e7aff8f65ee861720759d25068d286bc180a949` into base `a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7610545632400cd5f82fa392bb2676248312f305 && git checkout 7610545632400cd5f82fa392bb2676248312f305
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30 1e7aff8f65ee861720759d25068d286bc180a949 && git checkout -B drift-repro a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30 && git merge --no-ff 1e7aff8f65ee861720759d25068d286bc180a949

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a74856df99ffc7dcbf7fb7ceaf31c5e746fcba30
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2f59522ae9b5213b228c051033c260a9947008ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-multi-replica-local-database.test.ts, packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-multi-node-gate-declaration.integration.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts (`declaresReplicasSharingState`), packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-ledger.ts (`sharesCloudBindingCredential`), packages/services/service-cluster/src/split-brain-guard.ts (`declaresMultiNode`), packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts (`inferDriverTypeFromUrl`, `resolveDriverType`, `resolveStorageDefinition`), packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts (`resolveStandaloneDatabase`), packages/cli/src/utils/telemetry-datasource.ts (`standaloneTelemetryPrimary`, the precedent read over the same input), packages/drivers/driver-turso/README.md (replica mode). Prose faces read against the diff, not reviewed: the changeset, content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx, content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx. No `hits`: no published schema and no governed path in the diff.

Inputs: card #31928 body and all 5 comments (triage 6740652730, claim 6740655810, amendments 6740708364 and 6742846439, dev report 6742820815); PR #31954 body and file list (7 files); `git diff 2b880f12...2f59522a` (merge base 2b880f121d36); the head's 51 check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**What accept set narrows.** The set of environments `os serve` (and `os start`, which spawns it) boots on. Newly refused: `declaresReplicasSharingState(process.env)` is true, meaning `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` or `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` greater than 1 (`declaresMultiNode`), AND `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` trims to `redis`. On top of that, the resolved primary must be driver `sqlite`, `sqlite-wasm`, or `turso` over a URL that `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` classes as `sqlite`/`sqlite-wasm`. Such a boot now exits 1 with one `[database] Refusing to start: ...` line. Nothing widens: no flag, env key, route, error code or package export is added. `multiReplicaLocalDatabaseRefusal` and `MultiReplicaPrimaryDatabase` are module exports of `serve.ts`, and the CLI package publishes only its command classes.

**Who is reached.**
- A licensed (gate-admitted) multi-replica deploy over redis that kept its data in SQLite, using the default file, a `file:` URL or a path, or in sqlite-wasm or a libSQL `file:` URL. Before, it booted every replica on its own copy. Now it is refused.
- A gate-denied deploy that also set `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE=true` on a local database. Also newly refused.
- A gate-denied deploy on a local database without that hatch was already refused by the split-brain guard. It now gets the database refusal first, still with exit 1.
- Not reached: a single node, a declaration over any other cluster driver, and Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB and libSQL server URLs.

**Hazard (a): no false refusal.**
- The block runs only inside `if (await declaresReplicasSharingState(process.env))`.
- Postgres, MySQL and MongoDB fall through `localDatabaseKindOf` to `undefined`.
- `libsql://` and `https://*.turso.*` classify as `turso`, so they are not refused. That is pinned in the unit file, and its RED is shown by ablation 2.
- An explicit-turso `wss://` or plain `http://` server URL makes `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` throw `UnsupportedDriverError`. The `catch` returns `undefined`, so it is not refused (read in the code; not pinned).

**Hazard (b): every local form is caught.**
- `file:` URLs, absolute or relative, match `/^file:/i`, so they are `sqlite`.
- A bare path and `:memory:` match no scheme, so they are `sqlite`.
- `*.wasm.db` and `wasm-sqlite://` are `sqlite-wasm`.
- With no URL, the standalone resolver returns the unified-default file as `sqlite`. On the legacy route in dev, `resolveStorageDefinition` returns `sqlite` `:memory:`.
- On the legacy route in production with no URL, it resolves `null` and nothing is judged. That boot has no SQLite default to refuse.
- Driver ids come back canonical: `resolveExplicitDriver` uses `resolveDatabaseDriverId`, and `resolveStorageDefinition` returns `driverId` from the same kind. So no alias slips past the `=== 'sqlite'` test.
- libSQL replica mode (`file:` plus `syncUrl`) writes through Knex and better-sqlite3 to the local file (driver-turso README, "Local/Replica modes"). Refusing it is correct.

**Hazard (c): the undeclared path.**
- New on every boot: a static `import './start.js'` (no module-level side effects; `start.ts` does not import `serve.ts`, so there is no cycle), one lazy `import('@objectstack/cloud-connection')` (a hard dependency, `"sideEffects": false`), one pure boolean, and one local assignment.
- `resolveStandaloneDatabase` and the fallback resolution run only under the declaration. The standalone one is already run over the identical input by `standaloneTelemetryPrimary`, so it raises no new error even then.
- Nothing is printed off the declared path, so output is unchanged.

**Hazard (d): forced test edits.**
- Cases 1 and 3 keep every original assertion (gate denial with its no-gate reason, `GUARD_REFUSAL`, `booted === false`). Only the database moved, to `SHARED_DATABASE_ENV` (unreachable `mysql://127.0.0.1:9` plus `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE=true`).
- The escape hatch is the datasource's, not the guard's. `waitFor` still matches the guard's own words, so these cases still prove the split-brain refusal and are not weakened.
- `mysql://` is not local, so the new refusal cannot mask the guard in them.
- Case 4 keeps its gate assertions (`asked for 2`, no denial). It trades `booted === true` for the local-database refusal; see ④.
- Budget 40 to 58: eight boots, 45.86 s × 1.25 = 57.3, rounded up to 58. Consistent.

**Hazard (e): exit 1, nothing connected first.**
- `throw new Error(refusal)` lands in `run()`'s outer `catch`, which calls `printError(...)` and then `this.exit(1)`. The integration pin reads the child's own `exitCode === 1` for `file:`, the default and wasm.
- Before the block, the code only imports the cluster packages, constructs `Runtime` (registering, not connecting, the cluster plugin) and `kernel.use`s ObjectQL.
- No `listen`, `createServer` or driver connect appears between the boot's start and the refusal. Step 2's `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` and `runtime.start()` both come after it.

**Hazard (f): credentials.** The text is a fixed template with only the kind (`SQLite` / `SQLite (sqlite-wasm)` / `a libSQL file`) interpolated. The URL is never printed. Pinned by "names the variable and never the URL".

**Hazard (g): the helper change.** The `exitCode` addition to `ServeRun` is purely additive. Only `serve-boot-diagnostics-noise-budget.e2e.test.ts` names the type, and it never builds one. No test deep-equals a `runServe` result. `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` includes only `src`, so `test/` typing is unaffected.

**The dev's deviations.**
- Base RED by wiring ablation is acceptable: the unit function does not exist on `main`, and the ablation disables only the throw. It reports 3 failed integration cases, including the admitted-gate boot reaching `Server is ready` on SQLite, which is the defect itself.
- `git diff 2bf77f56 pr-31954` (the commit is reachable): exactly `+2` lines in `serve-multi-replica-local-database.test.ts`, a comment plus `import '@objectstack/cloud-connection'`. So the dogfood and full cli unit readings on `2bf77f56` carry to this head.
- The placement and file-surface deviations are seat-ruled in 6740708364 and 6742846439.
- The known limit (a host config whose own plugin registers the driver is not judged) is ruled out of scope and named in the PR body.

**Check-runs on the head:** 30 success, 14 skipped, 0 failure. Test Core shards 1–7 of 8 are `in_progress` (shard 8/8 success). `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check · *`, `Build Core` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are green.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. Correct per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` ruling A: the level follows `Metadata-protocol:` alone, and it reads `none` in both the PR body and the changeset. No author-facing protocol moves.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is at line start in both carriers, a well-formed declaration, and it decides the narrowing face.
- `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads the arm and `**BREAKING**` as breaking signals. The changeset answers with `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That is honest: no schema key and no stored row move, and the remedy is an operator's choice of database (an env value), not a rewrite of consumer code or metadata.
- The CI gate (`Check Changeset`, the lint gate lanes) is green on this head.
- No major and no `minor` is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- R3 holds. The change takes effect only under `declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis`'s pre-boot form, the single-node path is untouched, and the split-brain guard's code is untouched and still asserted by cases 1 and 3.
- The R2 shape holds: only the redis driver is in scope.
- No new error code (same shape as `start.ts`'s `MULTI_REPLICA_AUTH_SECRET_REFUSAL`), no new public name, no new URL parsing. The block reuses `resolveStandaloneDatabase`, `resolveDriverType` with `resolveStorageDefinition`, and `inferDriverTypeFromUrl`, matching the Step 0 rulings.
- The file surface matches the claim with both amendments. No out-of-surface file moved.
- No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.**
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` already states that "All replicas must share the same ... database". This refusal makes that stated requirement real at the consumer.
- The one contrary published claim, `kernel/cluster.mdx`'s "SQL / Turso / Postgres / SQLite all work the same" beside redis, is corrected in the same diff. So the capability withdrawn is one the spec's own rule already excluded, and it was silently corrupting (per-replica divergence).
- The `serve.ts` implementation agrees with its contract and its jsdoc: placement, gating, local kinds, a remedy naming a Postgres `OS_DATABASE_URL`, and no URL in the text.
- The changeset's BREAKING paragraph tells the reached operator what moved, what is printed, and the fix.

Findings:
- **should-fix**: Integration case 4. Its `expect(out).not.toContain(GUARD_REFUSAL)` is vacuous: the database refusal throws before `runtime.start()`, so the guard can never run there. The case has also lost its only proof that a gate-admitted declared boot completes. Boot it over `SHARED_DATABASE_ENV` (the escape hatch cases 1 and 3 already rely on) to keep `booted === true` and pin the new refusal only in the second `describe`. Or, if a degraded boot cannot complete, drop the vacuous line and say in the header that the admitted path's completion is no longer observable in this suite.
- **nit**: With a gate denial and a local database, the database refusal now pre-empts the guard's message. The gate's denial warning still prints and the exit is still 1, so R3 is not weakened, but the operator learns about the second refusal only after fixing the first. A clause in the refusal text or the docs saying that the cluster declaration is checked too would help.
- **nit**: The unit pin covers neither explicit-turso over `wss://` or `http://` server URLs (not refused) nor `:memory:` and relative `file:./` (refused). All four are decided by the reused classifier, but hazards (a) and (b) are unpinned for them.
- **nit**: `ServeRun.exitCode`'s doc says it is `null` when `runServe` stopped the child. A child that handles SIGTERM and exits on its own reports its code, for example 0. This is harmless: only self-exit paths read it.
- **nit**: The corrected `cluster.mdx` list ("Postgres, MySQL and a libSQL server") omits MongoDB, which is also not refused and is named in the changeset.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-multi-replica-local-database.test.ts, packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-multi-node-gate-declaration.integration.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts (`declaresReplicasSharingState`), packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-ledger.ts (`sharesCloudBindingCredential`), packages/services/service-cluster/src/split-brain-guard.ts (`declaresMultiNode`, `assertClusterDriverSafeForTopology`), packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts (`inferDriverTypeFromUrl`, `resolveDriverType`, `resolveStorageDefinition`), packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts (`resolveStandaloneDatabase`, `detectDriverFromUrl`), packages/cli/src/utils/telemetry-datasource.ts (`standaloneTelemetryPrimary`), packages/core/src/kernel.ts (Phase 1 init before Phase 2 start), packages/drivers/driver-turso/README.md (replica mode). Inputs:
- `git diff 2f59522a pr-31954`: one commit, `e07ef903`, touching 4 files (+37/−20): the unit pin, the integration harness, the `serve-process.ts` doc comment and `cluster.mdx`. `serve.ts` and the changeset are byte-identical to round 1.

- The check-runs on `e07ef903`.
- Card #31928 and its comments, as in round 1. No new seat ruling bears on the delta.

### ① Derived judgments

Everything round 1 derived about `serve.ts` carries over unchanged, because no source file moved. That covers:
- the accept set narrowed, and who is reached;
- hazards (a)–(c), (e) and (f);
- the undeclared path evaluating only a pure predicate.

`git diff 2bf77f56 pr-31954` names only `cluster.mdx`, the unit pin, the helper comment and the integration harness. So the dogfood and full cli unit readings on `2bf77f56` still carry, as the PR body says.

**What each round-1 item became:**

- **S1 (should-fix, case 4's vacuous guard line and lost completion proof): resolved, downgraded to a residual nit.**
  - Case 4 now boots over `SHARED_DATABASE_ENV`.
  - It drops `booted === true`, and the header documents why: the boot stops at the auth plugin's start, "No driver available for object 'sys_organization'". That is the round-1 alternative of saying so in the header.
  - It asserts `GATE_ASKED 2`, no `GATE_DENIAL`, no `LOCAL_DATABASE_REFUSAL` and no `GUARD_REFUSAL`.
- **What case 4 now proves, and whether it can fail:**
  - The gate admits a count-unknown declaration as 2 (two positive assertions that bite on a denying or mis-asked gate).
  - A shared `mysql://` primary is not refused locally. This bites if the classification ever counted MySQL as local, duplicating a unit row end to end.
  - The guard line is no longer structurally unreachable. The database refusal no longer fires, and `kernel.ts` runs every plugin's Phase-1 `init` (where `ClusterServicePlugin` calls the guard) before any Phase-2 `start` (where auth fails). So the guard executes before the boot dies.
  - Cases 1 and 3 boot over the identical database env and positively observe `GUARD_REFUSAL`. That proves this env reaches `ClusterServicePlugin.init`, so case 4's absence assertions are not satisfied by an earlier crash.
- **Residual:**
  - Case 4's `not.toContain(GUARD_REFUSAL)` is held by `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE=true`, not by the gate. The fixture's stand-in registers `redis` as `defineCluster({ driver: 'memory' })`, and the guard reads only the composed driver's NAME. So admission and denial both reach the guard as `memory`, and the hatch returns early either way. The line can fail only if the guard stopped honouring its own hatch.
  - This is the same property `main`'s case 4 had, since its `booted === true` was held by the same hatch. It is at parity, not weaker than `main`.
  - **To make it bite on the gate:** have the stand-in compose a driver that reports a non-`memory` name (it can still delegate to the memory primitives), and drop the hatch from case 4. Then a gate path that wrongly drops the remote driver falls back to `memory`, and the guard refuses: the absence assertion goes red. Alternatively, keep the hatch and positively assert a marker the stand-in prints when the `redis` driver is composed, proving admission kept the remote driver.
- **N2 (unit pin gaps): resolved.**
  - The diff is +8 lines because each line is one real table row in an `it.each`. Four rows are added to the refused table: `standalone(':memory:')`, `fallback(':memory:', 'turso')`, `standalone('file:./data/app.db')` and `standalone('file:./data/app.db', 'turso')`. Four are added to the not-refused table: `standalone`/`fallback` over `'wss://app-org.turso.io'` and `'http://127.0.0.1:8080'` with `'turso'`.
  - Count: round 1 had 10 + 1 refused and 7 not refused, so 18; now 14 + 1 refused and 11 not refused, so 26. The claim is exact.
  - Each row runs through the real resolution, and I traced the paths in code:
    - `detectDriverFromUrl(':memory:')` has no scheme, so it returns `sqlite`.
    - `file:./` matches `/^file:/i`.
    - Explicit `turso` keeps the driver.
    - `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` returns `sqlite` for `:memory:` and `file:./`, so those are refused. It throws `UnsupportedDriverError` for `wss://` and `http://` without a `.turso.` host; the `catch` returns `undefined`, so those are not refused.
  - The fallback rows are the "fallback" pair the coordinator named. The relative `file:./` rows are standalone only, which is a nit-sized asymmetry: the fallback goes through the same `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` regex.
  - The PR body reports a third ablation (the `catch` forced to refuse) with 4 failed and 22 passed, which is the RED for the new negative rows.
- **N4 (cluster.mdx omitted MongoDB): resolved.** The list now reads "Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB and a libSQL server", matching the changeset.
- **N3 (exitCode doc): resolved.** The comment now says the value is meaningful only for a child that exited on its own, and that a SIGTERM-handling child may report its own code, 0 included. It is test-only and type-identical.
- **Round-1 nit on the gate-denied, local-database message order: unchanged, still a nit.** No code moved. The refusal still pre-empts the guard's message under a gate denial on a local database; the exit is still 1 and R3 holds.

**Hazard (d), re-read on this head.**
- Cases 1 and 3 are unchanged.
- Case 4 now shares the cases' database env.
- The budget header stays 58 for the same eight boots.
- No split-brain assertion is weakened: cases 1 and 3 still positively require `GUARD_REFUSAL` with `booted === false`.

**Hazard (g).** `ServeRun` is unchanged in shape; only the doc moved.

**Check-runs on `e07ef903`:** 39 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure.
- All eight Test Core shards, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint and Type Check lane, and one `Check Changeset` run are green.
- A second `Check Changeset` run is `in_progress`; this matches a re-run after the body edit.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1. The changeset is byte-identical:
- `'@objectstack/cli': patch` follows `Metadata-protocol: none`, per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` ruling A.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is at line start in the PR body and the changeset.
- The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest, because the remedy is an operator's choice of database.
- No `major` or `minor` is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Unchanged:
- R3 holds, with the effect only under the declaration and the guard untouched.
- No new error code, public name or URL parsing.
- The delta stays inside the amended file surface: tests, the test helper and `cluster.mdx`.
- No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing still makes the published "All replicas must share the same ... database" rule real at the consumer, and the one contrary published claim in `cluster.mdx` is corrected, now with MongoDB listed too. `serve.ts` agrees with its contract, as judged in round 1.

Findings:
- **nit (residual of S1)**: Case 4's `not.toContain(GUARD_REFUSAL)` is held by `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE`, not the gate, at parity with `main`. Make it bite by having the fixture's stand-in report a non-`memory` driver name and dropping the hatch, or by positively asserting a stand-in marker that the `redis` driver was composed.
- **nit**: The relative `file:./` rows are pinned on the standalone path only. The fallback reads the same `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` regex.
- **nit (carried)**: Under a gate denial with a local database, the database refusal pre-empts the guard's message. The exit is still 1 and R3 is not weakened.

No must-fix. No should-fix.
